notes: C1 and C2 have empty Held Lines in CONCEPTS even though the RTL stores their values in rtx_engine.sreg and the FIFO paths at lines 244, 292 and 318.
The bus request and response record fields are reported as structural secondaries where they carry or control a conceptual asset, but their record nature prevents primary status.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> tx_fifo.wdata carries bus_req_i.data.
points.reason: The bus data directly sets the transmit FIFO write data, so it can modify the payload, but this internal write-data point has no readout.

points.reached by: tx_fifo.wdata ==> tx_fifo_inst carries the transmit write data through the FIFO input.
points.reason: Under the black-box FIFO assumption, the write data can alter the stored transmit word and the FIFO returns it on rdata_o, but the instance has no direct external payload observation.

points.reached by: Backward influence from tx_fifo_inst follows tx_fifo.re ==> tx_fifo_inst, whose read control selects whether the payload is returned.
points.reason: This signal only controls FIFO reading and does not itself expose or modify the payload under the objectives listed for this concept.

points.reached by: tx_fifo_inst ==> transceiver carries tx_fifo.rdata into the transceiver.
points.reason: The FIFO word is loaded into and shifted through sreg, which can be read through spi_dat_o and can be changed by the transceiver's load and shift assignments.

points.reached by: transceiver ==> spi_dat_o carries rtx_engine.sreg to the output assignment.
points.reason: The output directly exposes the current transmit shift-register bit; this assignment provides observation but no external write mechanism.

points.reached by: spi_dat_i ==> transceiver carries the serial input into the receive sampling logic.
points.reason: The serial input is sampled into sdi_sync and shifted into sreg, which is later stored in the receive FIFO and returned through the bus response.

points.reached by: transceiver ==> rx_fifo.wdata carries rtx_engine.sreg into the receive FIFO write-data logic.
points.reason: The received shift-register value is assigned to the FIFO write data and can therefore be changed by the sampled serial input and later read out.

points.reached by: rx_fifo.wdata ==> rx_fifo_inst carries the received word through the FIFO input.
points.reason: Under the black-box FIFO assumption, the write data is stored and returned by rdata_o, so the received payload can be altered at the input and observed through the return path.

points.reached by: Backward influence from rx_fifo_inst follows bus_req_i --> rx_fifo.re and rx_fifo.re ==> rx_fifo_inst, where the read control selects the returned data.
points.reason: The read-enable logic controls when the FIFO word is consumed but does not itself expose or alter the received payload.

points.reached by: rx_fifo_inst ==> bus_access carries rx_fifo.rdata into the bus response logic.
points.reason: The receive FIFO data is copied into bus_rsp_o.data, providing a direct software-visible observation path without a payload modification at this block.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> bus_access carries bus_req_i.data into the control-register write logic.
points.reason: A bus write stores ctrl.enable, and reset or a value of zero can clear the state that enables SPI operation.

points.reached by: bus_access ==> rx_fifo.clear carries ctrl.enable through the clear assignment.
points.reason: The inverted enable directly drives FIFO clear inputs, so changing the enable state can clear or disable queued transfer data.

points.reached by: bus_access ==> tx_fifo.clear carries ctrl.enable through the clear assignment.
points.reason: The inverted enable directly drives the transmit FIFO clear input, allowing the enable state to clear pending transmit data.

points.reached by: rx_fifo.clear ==> rx_fifo_inst carries the enable-derived clear control into the receive FIFO.
points.reason: Under the black-box FIFO assumption, the clear input can reset or block the receive FIFO state when enable is removed.

points.reached by: tx_fifo.clear ==> tx_fifo_inst carries the enable-derived clear control into the transmit FIFO.
points.reason: Under the black-box FIFO assumption, the clear input can reset or block the transmit FIFO state when enable is removed.

points.reached by: bus_access --> clock_generator carries ctrl.enable as a condition controlling clock generation.
points.reason: The enable condition clears the divider and prevents spi_clk_en from being generated, blocking SPI operation.

points.reached by: bus_access ==> transceiver carries ctrl.enable into the transceiver state assignment.
points.reason: ctrl.enable directly sets a state bit, so a bus write can change the engine mode and disable normal transfer sequencing.

points.reached by: bus_access ==> irq_generator carries ctrl.enable into the interrupt-enable expression.
points.reason: The enable is an outer gate on irq_o, so clearing it can suppress interrupt activity needed for operation.

points.reached by: bus_access ==> clkgen_en_o reaches the concurrent output assignment.
points.reason: This output reflects the enable state but the output assignment itself provides no additional observation or influence mechanism.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> bus_access carries bus_req_i.data into the clock-configuration register writes.
points.reason: Bus writes store the prescaler, divider and high-speed settings, and an unsuitable value can later prevent correctly paced operation.

points.reached by: bus_access --> clock_generator carries ctrl.cdiv, ctrl.enable, ctrl.highspeed and ctrl.prsc as clock-generation controls.
points.reason: The configuration controls the divider comparison and the generation of spi_clk_en, so the clock-generation logic can stall or mispace transfer steps.

points.reached by: clock_generator --> transceiver carries spi_clk_en as the pacing condition for transfer states.
points.reason: The generated enable gates state advancement and serial clock updates, so its absence prevents the configured transfer pacing from operating.

points.reached by: bus_req_i ==> tx_fifo.wdata carries the command data into the transmit FIFO.
points.reason: The bus command word directly sets the FIFO input, allowing the selected target or active state to be changed or made ineffective.

points.reached by: tx_fifo.wdata ==> tx_fifo_inst carries the chip-select command into the FIFO instance.
points.reason: Under the black-box FIFO assumption, the command can be stored incorrectly and returned to the transceiver, selecting the wrong or no target.

points.reached by: tx_fifo_inst ==> transceiver carries tx_fifo.rdata to the chip-select command decode.
points.reason: The queued command conditionally loads cs_ctrl, while the other-state branch clears it, so the transceiver can select the wrong device or no device.

points.reached by: transceiver ==> bus_access carries rtx_engine.cs_ctrl into the selected-device readback.
points.reason: This block only reports cs_ctrl in the response word and does not itself alter the selected-device state.

points.reached by: transceiver --> chip_select carries rtx_engine.cs_ctrl as the selection condition and index.
points.reason: The process drives all chip-selects inactive and asserts the indexed line only when cs_ctrl(3) is set, so selection can be wrong, absent, or reset.

points.reached by: holding block; bus_access, rx_fifo_inst, tx_fifo_inst and rtx_engine.busy feed the interrupt expression.
points.reason: The process computes and registers irq_o from enable, interrupt-selection bits, FIFO status and engine busy state, so those conditions can create or suppress an interrupt.

points.reached by: Backward influence follows bus_access ==> irq_generator for the interrupt-selection and enable fields.
points.reason: Bus writes change ctrl.enable and the interrupt-selection registers, allowing interrupt generation to be altered or disabled.

points.reached by: Backward influence follows rx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator for rx_fifo.avail.
points.reason: Under the black-box FIFO assumption, its availability output affects the interrupt condition and can therefore make the indication incorrect or absent.

points.reached by: Backward influence follows tx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator for tx_fifo.avail and tx_fifo.half.
points.reason: Under the black-box FIFO assumption, its empty and half-full outputs determine interrupt conditions and can cause or suppress the indication.

points.reached by: Backward influence follows rtx_engine.busy ==> irq_generator for the idle-interrupt condition.
points.reason: The derived busy state is an operand of the idle interrupt condition, so an incorrect busy value can produce a spurious or missing interrupt.
